arms.anchor: Per symbol, at end of day t-1: if |disp[t-1]| >= rolling 60-day 80th percentile of |disp|, hold position -sign(disp[t-1]) over day t (1-day hold, FADE of the displacement); else flat. Unit notional per active symbol-day; entry fill at last_price[t-1] (decision instant), exit at last_price[t]; both symbols may be simultaneously active.
arms.neighbour: Same mechanism, different parameters, exact numbers: trigger threshold = rolling 90-day 75th percentile of |disp|, 1-day hold, identical fill/sizing convention (wider estimation window, looser quantile — parameter sensitivity of the displacement fade).
arms.control: Exposure-form placebo, exact spec: identical book machinery conditioned instead on |ret_z[t-1]| >= rolling 60-day 80th percentile of |ret_z|, position -sign(ret_z[t-1]), 1-day hold — plain volatility-normalized short-term reversal; identical costs, folds, gates.

features.name: vwap
features.role: conditioning input: volume-clock average price of day t-1

features.name: last_price
features.role: conditioning input: time-clock terminal print of day t-1; also entry/exit fill price

features.name: high_price
features.role: conditioning input: range normalization of day t-1

features.name: low_price
features.role: conditioning input: range normalization of day t-1

features.name: derived disp[t] = (last_price[t] - vwap[t]) / (high_price[t] - low_price[t])
features.role: close-to-VWAP displacement, dimensionless; divergence between the volume clock (VWAP) and the time clock (terminal print), normalized by the day's own range; derived from staged columns only

features.name: derived ret_z[t] = (last_price[t]/last_price[t-1] - 1) / rolling_60d_std(daily returns)
features.role: CONTROL-ARM-ONLY exposure: prior-day volatility-normalized return; derived from staged columns only

frozen_families.causal_claim: Benchmark-driven passive flow (VWAP/TWAP execution desks and daily-candle mark users) is forced to complete near the UTC day boundary, so when a day's terminal print sits far from that day's volume-weighted average price relative to the day's range, scheduled completion flow rather than informed flow has displaced price off its volume anchor and the displacement mean-reverts over the next session; the mechanism must fail when late-day prints carry informed directional content (displacement persists instead of reverting) or once the public price-shape pattern is crowded.
frozen_families.falsification_rule: The claim is proven wrong if any of: (a) after cost, the fade of extreme prior-day |displacement| earns non-positive expectancy (frozen rule order #1, G1 anchor FAIL); (b) the raw prior-return-fade exposure-form control reproduces the anchor (same sign, >= 0.5x anchor expectancy) — proving the displacement variable adds no information beyond short-term reversal (G11 falsification-by-control fires); (c) the measured sign is robustly opposite (displacement continues rather than reverts across >= 2 folds); or (d) G12 pooled ancestry |rho| > 0.20 vs any forbidden family or measured shadow at D2.
frozen_families.expected_failure_mode: Control-identifiability: displacement shares most of its variation with the prior day's signed return, so the measured anchor-vs-control exposure correlation at D2 plausibly exceeds the 0.20 bar and the family dies as a relabelled reversal ancestor; secondarily, crowding of a public price-shape regularity and fold concentration (the p80 trigger yields a thin event book of roughly 60 active symbol-days per symbol).
frozen_families.control_class: raw-level/exposure-form placebo (mandatory for conditioning-variable claims per FAMILY_PIPELINE section 3 step 11): the identical quantile-fade book conditioned instead on the prior day's volatility-normalized return z-score — the convenient explanation 'day-boundary displacement is just short-term reversal' must NOT reproduce the anchor; fully panel-runnable under evidenced semantics (all control inputs are staged price columns). Sham-calendar is deliberately NOT the mandated class and the V5 lesson is addressed head-on: the conditioning variable is a within-interval price-shape ratio, not a calendar event — the UTC boundary only defines the aggregation interval and no day-of-week/session/holiday term enters the rule.

arms.anchor: Per symbol, at end of day t-1: if |run_imb[t-1]| >= rolling 60-day 80th percentile of |run_imb|, hold position sign(run_imb[t-1]) over day t (1-day hold, CONTINUATION of the run side); else flat. Unit notional per active symbol-day; entry fill at last_price[t-1] (decision instant), exit at last_price[t]; both symbols may be simultaneously active.
arms.neighbour: Same mechanism, different parameters, exact numbers: trigger threshold = rolling 90-day 75th percentile of |run_imb|, 1-day hold, identical fill/sizing convention (wider estimation window, looser quantile — parameter sensitivity of run-persistence continuation).
arms.control: Reshuffled-interval placebo, exact spec: apply the identical anchor rule to run_imb with day labels permuted within 2025-10-21..2026-08-21 under numpy default_rng(seed=16), ONE fixed permutation shared by both symbols (a 200-permutation dispersion band is declared as a diagnostic output only, never as the bookable control); identical costs, folds, gates.

features.name: buy_streak_max
features.role: conditioning input: longest consecutive taker-buy print run of day t-1

features.name: sell_streak_max
features.role: conditioning input: longest consecutive taker-sell print run of day t-1

features.name: derived run_imb[t] = (buy_streak_max[t] - sell_streak_max[t]) / (buy_streak_max[t] + sell_streak_max[t])
features.role: signed run-side skew of the print sequence, in (-1, 1); a within-day ratio, count-normalized by construction — measures the SIDE-SHAPE of the aggressive sequence, not its net direction; derived from staged columns only

features.name: last_price
features.role: entry/exit fill price only (no conditioning role)

frozen_families.causal_claim: An extreme maximal same-side aggressor run on day t reflects order-splitting execution algorithms (or cascade engines) still mid-parent-order at the day boundary, and a split parent order is slow to complete and forced to keep taking liquidity in the same direction into the next session, so extreme run-side days see next-day same-direction continuation; the mechanism must fail when run extremes are end-of-day single-print artifacts or intraday liquidation cascades that fully mean-revert before the next session.
frozen_families.falsification_rule: The claim is proven wrong if any of: (a) after cost, the continuation book earns non-positive expectancy (frozen rule order #1, G1 anchor FAIL); (b) the day-label-permuted reshuffled-interval control reproduces the anchor (same sign, >= 0.5x anchor expectancy) — the t to t+1 alignment of run shape carries no next-day information (G11 fires); (c) the measured sign is robustly OPPOSITE the claimed continuation direction across >= 2 folds (the claim's direction is wrong, not merely unprofitable); or (d) G12 pooled ancestry |rho| > 0.20 vs any forbidden family, recorded ancestor, or measured shadow at D2.
frozen_families.expected_failure_mode: Mechanical streak inflation: maximal run length grows with daily print count, so on high-activity days the conditioning variable degenerates toward a volume/activity-level proxy — the mined dollar-volume-shock axis (XSECT-VOLSHK ancestry) — and the family dies at D2 (rho vs activity-form exposures) or at G4 fold concentration because activity regimes cluster in time; secondarily, crowding of a public run-persistence regularity; the shared aggressor-sign ancestry with M01-AGGRESSOR-ABSORPTION is the accepted rho risk the family is willing to lose to.
frozen_families.control_class: reshuffled-interval placebo (mandatory for temporal-structure claims per FAMILY_PIPELINE section 3 step 11), in the only semantics runnable on the panel-only surface: permute the DAY-INDEX alignment of the conditioning series within the post-warmup span and run the identical continuation book — this destroys the t to t+1 pairing while preserving the marginal exposure distribution. A within-day sign-sequence shuffle is infeasible because per-print signs are not staged in the daily panel; that constraint is disclosed here rather than papered over (P-3: a control that cannot run under evidenced semantics is a design failure — this one runs).
